chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man drinks the fermented Nabidh, his testimony is not valid in anything (regarding drinks), even if he were described as being upon the belief that you are upon.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَة: Testimony, witnesshood in legal or religious contexts.
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh, a drink made by soaking raisins or dates in water, often slightly fermented.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the testimony of someone who drinks fermented Nabidh?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the specific legal consequence of consuming *Nabidh al-makhmur* (fermented grape/date water), distinguishing it from general intoxication. The Imam emphasizes that even if the individual is theologically sound (*mu'taqad bihi*), their testimony (*shahada*) is invalidated in matters concerning beverages, highlighting a precise jurisprudential nuance where consumption of this specific drink renders one *fasiq* for the purpose of witness validity. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical act of consumption and its immediate impact on legal standing, regardless of the drinker's doctrinal correctness.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Bakr Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man drinks Al-Nabeez, the fermented, so his testimony is not allowed in anything (when he consumes from the drinks of intoxicants), even if he were to be described to be upon (the belief) that you are upon’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Bakr ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one drinks intoxicating al-Nabidh his testimony is not acceptable in any of the drinks, even if he believes in what you believe.’”
